property_summary: When non-owner calls owned(), reference version succeeds silently while bug version reverts because modifier condition is inverted.

The reference contract allows a non-owner to call transferOwnership because the onlyOwner modifier uses require(msg.sender == owner), which correctly ensures only the owner can call it; the second version has a bug where require(msg.sender != owner) allows any non-owner to call transferOwnership, so after deploy, owner is address(0), and a call from any EOA (e.g., address(1)) reverts in the reference (fails assertion) but succeeds in the buggy version (passes assertion).

With owner initially set, a call to transferOwnership(msg.sender) in the reference version keeps owner unchanged, while the buggy version sets owner to address(0) — assertEq(c.owner(), address(0x1)) holds for the reference but fails for the buggy version.
After Alice (the initial owner) calls transferOwnership(Bob), the reference version sets owner to Bob, but the buggy version sets owner to address(0).
After owner calls transferOwnership(address(0x1)), the reference sets owner to 0x1, but the buggy version sets owner to address(0).

After transferring ownership to a new address, the new owner calls owned() and it succeeds (no revert) in the reference, but reverts in the buggy version because the ownership transfer was commented out.
When transferOwnership is called by the owner, the reference sets owner to the newOwner argument, while the bug sets owner to msg.sender (the caller), causing owner to remain unchanged.
After calling transferOwnership with a new owner, the owner should be the new owner, not the original caller.
After transferring ownership with transferOwnership, the owner should be the new address passed as argument, not msg.sender.

Alice (non-owner) calls owned(), then Bob (initial owner) calls transferOwnership(Alice). In the reference, ownership transfers to Alice; in the buggy version, owner becomes msg.sender (Bob) instead. After the transfer, only the reference allows Alice to call owned() without revert.

After initial ownership is set via the constructor (owner is address(0)), Alice calls transferOwnership(address(0x1)). In the reference, owner becomes 0x1; in the buggy version, owner becomes msg.sender (Alice's address 0xAb5801a7D398351b8bE11C439e05C5B3259aeC9B), not 0x1. Reading the public owner variable shows the divergence.
